overall: Atlanta had a hot and humid afternoon with temperatures climbing steadily to a peak running max of 91.4°F around 16:00-17:00 ET, well above NWP model guidance. A sharp convective crash followed — temperatures plummeted from ~89-90°F to 80.6°F by 17:52 ET as the Severe Thunderstorm Watch/Warnings materialized in the region. By 18:52 ET temperatures had partially rebounded to 82.4°F but remain far below the day's peak, with ongoing thunderstorm activity and evening hours making any new high extremely unlikely.
forecast_obs_notes: All NWP models (ECMWF 87.5°F, HRRR 90.1°F, NBM 86.8°F) undershot the actual observed running max of 91.4°F; the HRRR was closest but still missed by ~1.3°F. The INTRADAY model strongly anchors at 90-91°F (96.8% probability) consistent with the 91.4°F running max sitting squarely in that 2-degree bucket, while the META model splits probability between 90-91°F and 92-93°F — but given the storm-driven temperature crash and no remaining heating window, the upper tail of META appears too generous.
max_temp_prediction: The daily high has almost certainly already been set at 91.4°F, recorded around 16:00-17:00 ET before the convective crash. With the current temperature at 80.6°F, zero upward velocity, evening hours, and active thunderstorms suppressing any solar recovery, there is essentially no path to a new daily maximum. Confidence is very high (>95%) that TMAX lands at 91.4°F or within a rounding margin of ±0.2°F of that value.
